newsitem.title: THAILAND: Arrests of Burma opposition leaders rise to 60.
newsitem.headline: Arrests of Burma opposition leaders rise to 60.

text.p: The number of senior members of Aung San Suu Kyi's party who have been arrested by Burma's military government has risen to about 60 and more arrests are expected, a senior NLD official said on Thursday.

The official told Reuters by telephone from Rangoon that the senior members of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party were detained by authorities as they headed to the Burmese capital to attend a party meeting.
"It is more than 60 now, I believe," the NLD official told Reuters from Suu Kyi's house. Most of those arrested were members of parliament (MPs) elected in a May 27, 1990, election.

The NLD won a landslide victory with more than 80 percent of the seats in the 1990 poll. But the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) never recognised the result and has cracked down on elected MPs and top party organisers ever since.

The party official said the NLD would go ahead with its plan to hold an anniversary celebration, which would double as a party meeting, on May 27. "We are a political party, and we have to do our job," he said.

More than 261 top NLD members, mostly elected MPs, were arrested in connection with a party congress planned to coincide with the anniversary last year. The SLORC said they only detained them temporarily for questioning to prevent anarchy. Many were later released.
